title: Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment Bill 2013
portfolio: Regional Australia, Local Government, Arts and Sport

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give the Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly power to determine its own membership size through territory legislation, removing the Commonwealth regulation step.
Any law setting, changing or repealing the Assembly’s membership number would need support from at least two-thirds of the total membership, rather than only members present.
The Assembly would remain at 17 members until it legislated a different number, and the revised mechanism would commence on the day following Royal Assent.
changes: The requirement for Commonwealth regulations to alter Assembly size would be repealed.
The special majority rule would extend to amendments and repeals of laws setting membership numbers.
The existing number of 17 members would operate as the default until a territory enactment provided otherwise.
summary.affected: The Australian Capital Territory Legislative Assembly and its members are affected.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported the Australian Capital Territory (Self-Government) Amendment Bill 2013 on Canberra's centenary, recounted that residents voted 63½ per cent against self-government in a 1978 plebiscite before the Hawke government granted it in 1988, and noted the first elected Legislative Assembly began with 18 members in 1974 compared with 17 today.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Marked Canberra's centenary, noted the Australian government has contributed $20 million to National Arboretum visitor facilities, argued using a cube root population rule the ACT assembly of 17 members is undersized compared with a suggested minimum of 25 MLAs, and paid tribute to the late ACT and Region Chamber of Commerce chief executive Chris Peters, who died on 27 February this year.
